name: Southern Blackberry
caution: No toxic look-alikes; the only hazards are thorns and the chiggers in the patch. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Upright thorny canes, unlike the ground-running dewberry. Pick fruit that is fully dull-black and releases at a touch; red means wait.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: The archetypal wild berry. Eat them warm off the cane, or bake the survivors into a cobbler.
